title: Pinball Dungeon Crawl
pitch: Real pinball, roguelike runs: break mobs for gold, shoot a cave, ride the rail down into a dungeon table, and reach the dragon in 15 minutes.

topics.title: Pitch
topics.summary: Real pinball, roguelike runs: break mobs for gold, shoot a cave, ride the rail down into a dungeon table, and reach the dragon in 15 minutes.

topics.title: Player Fantasy
topics.summary: A tiny wizard searching for an evil tome, the wizards' dangerous spellbook, stolen and held by an evil dragon.

topics.title: Pillars
topics.summary: 1. Never out of sight. 2. Every hit matters: real weight, always a step toward a goal. 3. Pure pinball: physics untouched, flippers only; the RPG happens in the abstract.

topics.title: Audience
topics.summary: Pinball people first, plus some roguelike die-hards. A short-to-medium game. When needs clash, make it feel like pinball.

topics.title: References
topics.summary: Yoku's Island Express is close, but that's a side-scroller. This looks and works like a real pinball machine, and is very mechanical.

topics.title: Core Loop
topics.summary: Shoot, break mobs (red drop targets) for gold. A quest spawns new mobs; break the ones in front of a cave and it opens. Shoot a cave to pick that dungeon, ride its rail down, beat the encounter, hit 1 of 3 loot targets or exit, ride the return rail back up, next quest.

topics.title: Core Mechanics
topics.summary: Pure pinball. Each flipper carries 1 item; the ball carries that item's effect from the moment the flipper hits it until the other flipper does. Items stay until replaced or a drain wipes both (the guardian ward breaks when it saves). Picking loot replaces the item on the last flipper to touch the ball; exiting takes nothing. Kinds: damage, elements, gold, control. Doubles don't stack. Prototype set: iron sword (+1 damage), fire staff (armor hits count double), coin purse (2 gold a break), guardian ward (saves one drain).

topics.title: Controls & Feel
topics.summary: Flippers only. No extra button: spells and weapons come from the flipper items; the only passive is the amulet holding your lives.

topics.title: Goals
topics.summary: Complete 3 tiered dungeons in order, ending at the dragon's lair. Light quests open each dungeon and can change the field or open micro dungeons.

topics.title: Challenge
topics.summary: Basic mobs break in 1 hit, like real drop targets. Armor is extra hits taken first and pays no gold until it's gone: a metal plate shows it and pops off, lamps in front show what's left, on bosses too (not on the display). Damage items count on armor too (+1 damage takes 2 points off anything). A tier 1 boss takes about 5 hits. Shot order changes with your loadout, mob weak spots and ordered puzzles. Tiers get tougher by a mix of armor, health and harder shots: each layout leans on a different one, at a similar level.

topics.title: Failure & Recovery
topics.summary: Permadeath: 1 wizard, 3 lives from the amulet; an item or two can add a life. Any drain, including in a dungeon, costs a life and wipes both flipper items and gold. Next ball, same map.

topics.title: Progression
topics.summary: No XP. Progress is dungeon completion, which unlocks the next tier, plus loot. Early items are simple benefits, never wrong to hit; higher-level loot can be game changers.

topics.title: Rewards & Economy
topics.summary: Every mob break pays 1 gold; trees pay nothing, nor do hits on armor. Gold only buys shop items, and a drain loses all of it. 3 shops: one cheap (about 3), one mid (about 6), one dear (about 10); shoot the one you can afford, the ball is held, press a flipper to equip it on that side. Shops restock after each dungeon. Dungeon loot is 1 of 3 choices or none, from the same pool as the shops.

topics.title: Setting
topics.summary: Classic heroic fantasy, like the airbrushed backglass of an 80s fantasy table. A fantasy world that's only shown as a machine; nobody in it knows. The main table is a ruined kingdom's countryside: ruins among the trees (the kingdom's old alchemy herbs, lore only), a town of an inn and 3 shops, caves into the kingdom's buried halls, the dragon's peak at the back. The dragon stole the wizards' dangerous spellbook, the tome.

topics.title: Story
topics.summary: Told by dot-matrix text and table changes. After dungeon 2 the dragon returns to its lair: landscape ruined, flames, 2 random town buildings destroyed and 2 left open, new trash mobs, a quick trick shot opens the boss cave into the lair, one of its 3 layouts at random.

topics.title: Characters
topics.summary: The ball is the tiny wizard. The evil dragon holds the tome.

topics.title: World & Level Structure
topics.summary: Built vertically: the main table on top, dungeon tables below it like a basement. 3 caves on the main table, each opened by breaking the mobs in front of it; a rail drops the ball into its dungeon. The cave picks the type: each leads to one of the current tier's 3 types. The lair is the exception: a trick shot opens the boss cave only, and its layout is random. Each dungeon has its own flippers and an exit sealed until the encounter is beaten. Every exit pipes back up through the top of the boss cave, then wire rails run down the left and right to the inlanes. Town block is an inn + 3 shops. 3 dungeons per run. Table sizes are drafts. The main table has 2–3 hand-made layouts; each run picks one.

topics.title: Opposition
topics.summary: Mobs are the red drop targets; trees are bumpers in the way, not enemies. Bosses fight in 2 phases: they move and dodge, then at half health drop their guard and a shield of targets goes up. They fight back only by changing the table (a post rises, a lane closes, a blocker drops), never the physics. Random encounters on the main table: mostly surprise mob waves, sometimes a wandering mini boss. Tier 1 goblin warren: break 3 goblins. Tier 2 crypt: hit 4 skeletons in order, a wrong one raises them all. Lair layout A: the dragon dodges on its hoard, then 4 scale targets shield it. The dragon is the final boss, with 3 lair layouts using different mini bosses and trash mobs.

topics.title: Art Direction
topics.summary: Looks like a real 3D pinball machine, very mechanical: metal wire rails, tables stacked vertically, rails going transparent as the ball travels. Pieces so far: tree bumpers, cave mouths, the dragon on its hoard, a dragon toy on the boss cave that snaps at the ball coming back up.

topics.title: Audio & Music
topics.summary: All real old-school pinball sounds.

topics.title: UI & HUD
topics.summary: A dot-matrix display above the table, like a real backbox. At rest it shows score, gold, lives and the current quest; events (breaks, shops, loot, quests) take it over for a few seconds. Each flipper shows its item as a color on the bat; names and details go on the display. No overlay: if something doesn't fit the display, simplify the game. Boss health shows on the toy (plate and lamps), not the display.

topics.title: Camera
topics.summary: Whole main table on screen. Entering a dungeon: the rail turns transparent, camera follows and zooms as the ball rolls in from the top side, showing the table for 2-3 seconds, then settles into a pinball view.

topics.title: Onboarding
topics.summary: The first quest teaches it: dot-matrix says something like BREAK THE GOBLINS, targets flash, first dungeon is easy. The rest is introduced one piece at a time.

topics.title: Session Shape
topics.summary: About 15 minutes for a full run. Unlike real pinball there's a goal that ends the game, so the player is trying to finish, not just last. Losing all 3 lives ends the run. Score: pinball points for every hit all run, plus bonuses for each dungeon cleared, lives left and beating the dragon.

topics.title: Replayability
topics.summary: Each run: random loot, shop stock and encounters; 3 dungeon types per tier, picked by cave; the main table is one of 2–3 hand-made layouts. Between runs: a high-score table and unlocks (new items in the pool, new dungeon types). Power never carries over.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.summary: Prototype baseline: only two buttons, remappable keys, ball speed option, and a dim mode that softens the machine lights.

topics.title: Platform & Tech
topics.summary: Godot, with the pinball physics as a C++ extension. Each table is its own 2D physics plane drawn in 3D; only the playfield is simulated. Ramps, rails and drops between tables are scripted paths. Builds for PC and the web (itch.io), so a portfolio visitor can play in one click.

topics.title: Scope & MVP
topics.summary: Full idea stays the vision. First prototype: one main table, one dungeon, a few flipper items; no terraforming or dragon. Tests hit feel, rail drop and camera, loot choice.

topics.title: Business Model
topics.summary: Free portfolio piece: both the design docs and the prototype.

topics.title: Risks
topics.summary: Physics feel, camera work, content load (9 unique dungeon tables), terraforming breaking tables.
